text:
HHS! MAT361 review!
So basically, with the end of this semester, I wrapped up my 3rd year at NSU. For the first time, I am writing a worst review of a worst faculty. I have never seen this worst of a faculty in my whole student life, not at NSU, not in school-college, not even in kindergarten! 
With due respect, he is a faculty at NSU, he might have all the qualifications best of the best, but teaching ain’t his profession. A person like him, can be in any profession, but not a noble work like teaching. A teacher is supposed to be a mentor, a person who motivates you, a person who makes you feel confident, but he is quite the opposite of what actually a teacher should be. From the very first day of the semester, "uni private er students der students e mone koren na, emon attitude." 
With due respect, he is a total psycho, sorry to use this word, but it is what it is, indeed. Throughout the whole semester, he literally tortured us, traumatised us. He makes sure that everyone feel low, demotivated. He screams at the students as his lungs out, and that ain’t a normal behaviour. Totally abnormal. Those who were in those section of MAT361, section 4 and section 6, each n every students agree at this one point. The environment that he created, is undefinable in words, only who experienced that knows better. Only 5-7 students attended his regular classes, so you can guess, what kinda environment he created. Only 15 students sit for the final exam. 
Now here comes his teaching part. First of all, his lectures ain’t well organised. He writes on the white board, "jokhon jekhane mon chay jebhabe iccha likhe, you need to find out on your own ki likhtese, koi theke koi likhte chole gelo." 
And we are clueless, what he is actually teaching. 
"Unar pora uni nijei bujhe." Unar slides are so so confusing, slides e ki shob random jinish poracche reading, and then suddenly uni R language open kore ki ki math dekhay jeta uni nijei jane, bujhe. Department theke bola ache ekta book follow korte, uni duita boi poray. Since this is a math course, isn’t it normal to expect to solve maths from the book chapter’s exercise problems? No!!!! He just teaches the basic concept (jeta o thik moto bujha jay na) and solve a problem from his slides and boom you are on your own! With a boat in the middle of an Ocean! What other math courses are like? Every faculty makes sure that you study and practice maths from the book chapter, so they specifically mention book problems. But he doesn’t even provide any suggestion even before the midterm and final. He doesn’t even mention je amra ashole koi theke math korbo, let the specific number away! In the last class of the semester, we requested him to give us at least some practice problems that we can at least take a preparation, he said he will provide us some practice problems. But he did not, he did the same in the midterm. He also said, he will provide us formula sheet in the final exam, uni seta o deyni. He breaks his commitment every time. He solves some basic math problems, but in the exam he intentionally makes the question harder, so that most of the students could not pass in the exam. He literally took this as a challenge, he also said, no students from the two sections combined would pass, he literally challenged. How can a faculty behaves like this with his students? In the final exam, he screamed his lungs out at two students, because they were only 2 minutes late. The way he screamed and the words that he uttered from his mouth, literally left us blank. I became so so nervous that my hands were shaking. As a result, exam went bad despite having a good preparation. During every exam, (quiz, midterm, final) he goes every student to student and standing in front of them, he checks what the student is writing in the answer script. If you’re writing something even though your math is correct, but you haven’t mentioned or defined the normal distribution(those who did mat361 will understand, this is just an example) or anything he just say "no matter what you write, you will get 0" this makes you nervous, even if you know the solution, you become nervous. I mean I just can’t define the situation. At the end of the semester, we, some of the students on behalf of the whole section, went to the Chairman Sir’s office to address all the problems that we had throughout the whole semester. Chairman Sir assured that he will take actions, we doubt that, rather HHS Sir is awarded with 4 sections of MAT361 this semester.
This review is to make the students aware of his nature and teaching style before taking mat361 under him. We just wasted our 20k and some valuable time taking this course under him. A lifelong lesson. I wish I could use some raw words to define his attitude towards the students. See less

Faculty Review: HHS
Course: MAT361
First i want to request to the group admin approve this post, it is important. Because students are going to face serious issue if not approved.
​This review is intended for junior students who are considering taking MAT361, in hopes of saving them from a highly traumatic experience.
​At the beginning of the semester, the instructor was pleasant. The concepts were manageable, and he taught accessible topics that we had already covered. He engaged the class with questions, we participated, and the sessions proceeded smoothly. The issues began when the more complex topics were introduced. A few days after the course drop deadline had passed, his demeanor drastically changed. He started delivering lectures without paying any attention to whether the students were comprehending the material. Furthermore, he used harsh language, claiming the topics were simple and expressing aggressive frustration over the students' inability to understand them.
​As the weeks progressed, his behavior became increasingly hostile. Many students had already dropped the course. His teaching became entirely incomprehensible. He selected difficult topics that were not in the prescribed textbook, outside the official syllabus, and non-compliant with NSU's faculty guidelines. He appeared entirely self-centered, expecting students to blindly adapt to his specific teaching methodology.
​When exams approached, he provided no guidance regarding the syllabus or the expected question formats. Students were left completely unaware of what to study amidst an overwhelmingly large syllabus, and he offered no assistance or clarification.
​Consequently, you learn very little and remain entirely unprepared for assessments. While some might find that tolerable, the midterm exam created immense pressure, especially for students who had multiple exams scheduled on the same day. The entire class politely requested a one-week postponement. In response, he became intensely angry. He yelled and threatened to fail everyone, screaming, "I will see how all of you pass the exam!" During the exam, he constantly paced around the hall—which was highly distracting—and scrutinized the room uncomfortably.
​Over time, the classes became exceedingly tedious. Attendance dwindled day by day, leaving fewer than 14 students by the end of the semester.
​During every exam, he shouted, screamed, and bullied students who arrived late, slightly moved their heads, or engaged in any trivial action. He never spoke politely. Instead, he constantly yelled and demotivated the class, stating that no one would pass and that he would personally ensure they failed. He genuinely seemed to view his students as adversaries.
​
​In conclusion, I strongly believe that this instructor exhibits signs of severe psychological instability. His lack of emotional regulation raised genuine concerns that he might even resort to physical violence against students. He is an emotionally unstable and rude individual, making it virtually impossible to successfully complete a course under his instruction. At the end of the semester, numerous students filed formal complaints against him with the department chair. Consequently, the chair instructed him to curve the grades based on the complaints. Nevertheless, it was a deeply traumatic experience. I highly doubt he will actually apply the curve, and his unpredictable question patterns and behavior remain absolutely unacceptable.
​He has been assigned three sections this upcoming semester. Before enrolling in his class, please consult students who have previously taken his courses. Almost everyone is aware of this situation and will echo the exact same sentiments. Thank you.
